question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $x=a$ is

$$
L(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

In our case, we have $a=36,$ which gives

$$
L(x)=f(36)+{f}^{′}(36)(x-36).
$$

Let's compute $f(36)$ and ${f}^{′}(36)$ in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get

$$
f(36)=\sqrt{36}=6,
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}},
$$

which in turn gives

$$
{f}^{′}(36)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{36}}=\frac{1}{2\cdot 6}=\frac{1}{12}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(36)+{f}^{′}(36)(x-36) \\  & =6+\frac{1}{12}(x-36) \\  & =6+\frac{1}{12}x-3 \\  & =6-3+\frac{1}{12}x \\  & =3+\frac{1}{12}x.\end{aligned}
$$
